title: Hal Puthoff on Rogan: US holds 15 crashed craft
summary: Jesse Michels tells of Hal Puthoff on Rogan: US holds 15 crashed craft, about 2025 at United States (no place named), and frames it as the host. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: Hal Putoff also went on Joe Rogan a few months ago and said, "We have 15 crash craft in our possession."
like you know if he's saying definitively the 12 to 15 >> crafts you know on on Joe Rogan it's like where are you getting that
tellings.difference: Gives the number as 12 to 15 rather than 15, and the teller doubts where Puthoff got it.
tellings.link_reason: Same story: Puthoff said on Joe Rogan's show that the US holds about 15 crashed craft.

tellings.quote: he he says that we have 10 to 40 crafts in our possession. He also says he worked with George W. Bush and Steven Hadley, his national security adviser, on, you know, whether we should make disclosures.
tellings.difference: Gives 10 to 40 craft instead of 15, and adds Puthoff's work with Bush and Hadley on disclosure.
tellings.link_reason: Puthoff's claim about how many crashed craft the US holds, credited to the Rogan appearance, is the same claim as the 15-craft story. The Bush/Hadley disclosure talks are tacked on as a second claim.

related.note: Both give a count of the crashed craft the US holds. Davis says fewer than 40, which differs from Puthoff's 15, so one count could be right and the other wrong.

plain: Jesse Michels, a podcast host, says that Hal Puthoff, a physicist long tied to government studies of unexplained phenomena, went on Joe Rogan's podcast in 2025 and said the US has 15 crashed craft in its possession. In a later episode Michels gives the number as 12 to 15 and wonders where Puthoff got such a definite figure. If true, it would mean the government holds a small fleet of non-human vehicles.
